<description>
Expose individual functional tests through the same CTest interface used for unit tests, making them easier to select, inspect, and rerun from the command line or CTest-aware IDEs.

Scheduling unit and functional tests together may improve parallel execution. It also enables per-test results and timings to be uploaded to our [Bitcoin Core CDash instance](https://my.cdash.org/index.php?project=bitcoin-core), helping track failures and runtime changes across builds.

Registration is opt-in with `BUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON` and requires CMake 4.4 or newer. The existing runner remains available for RPC coverage and CSV results. The native macOS CI job exercises the combined CTest workflow and passes. See `test/README.md` for usage and limitations.
</description>

<commits>
04764efd99 test: require full runner option names

bugfix where options such as --tmpdir can otherwise be consumed as
abbreviations of runner options.

Disable abbreviation so forwarding does not depend on which similarly
named runner options happen to exist.

0647078c66 test: expose functional cases to CTest

Reuse the existing selection and benchmark expansion before emitting the
inventory, so exclusions and child options have one source of truth.

Pass each test specification as one quoted argument to support multiple
variant options without imposing a fixed count.

Keep the existing skip and stderr failure semantics when CTest runs one
case. Share timeout and failure-log handling with cache setup, and leave
failed test directories intact across reruns.

7d3bbcffaa build: optionally register functional tests with CTest

Native discovery makes functional cases available to CTest scheduling,
filters and dashboards alongside unit tests. Require CMake 4.4 only when
this optional registration is enabled, avoiding a second discovery
implementation while retaining the existing minimum for normal builds.

Use fixtures to prepare the shared chain cache before parallel execution.
Run cache creation through the same Python wrapper as the test cases so
its timeout and failure handling cannot drift from theirs.

a44d018b32 ci: exercise functional CTest execution on macOS

Run unit and functional cases together in one native CI job to keep the
optional CTest path exercised.

Derive selection from the existing RUN_* switches and reuse the
sanitizer-wrapped invocation instead of adding another selection
interface.

Pass existing runner options through TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA, including
failure log output and the scratch directory. Exclude registered
functional cases from legacy unit-only CTest invocations to avoid
running them twice.

fd6ace0610 doc: explain optional functional CTest execution

Document the opt-in version requirement and standard selection commands
so developers can run individual cases or the combined suite. State the
remaining coverage and concurrent-invocation limits without implying a
replacement for every existing runner workflow.

f574198736 test: avoid CTest temporary directory collisions

Concurrent variants of the same script can observe the same wall-clock value
on macOS and select an identical temporary directory. The second test then
fails before framework setup completes.

Use a random UUID suffix so directory names do not depend on clock resolution.
Leave directory creation and cleanup with the test framework to preserve
failed logs and its requirement that the supplied path does not exist.
</commits>

index 0b34f52c1e..f92ee23076 100644
--- a/test/README.md

@@ -128,6 +128,53 @@ how many jobs to run, append `--jobs=n`
 The individual tests and the test_runner harness have many command-line
 options. Run `build/test/functional/test_runner.py -h` to see them all.
 
+#### CTest functional tests
+
+CTest registration is disabled by default, so the legacy runner remains the default local workflow. The macOS native CI job uses CTest; other CI jobs continue to use the legacy runner.
+Functional test registration uses CMake's native `discover_tests`, so it requires CMake 4.4 or newer. To enable it:
+
+```sh
+cmake -B build -DBUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON
+cmake --build build --parallel
+```
+
+An unfiltered `ctest` run includes unit tests and base functional tests. Pass `--extended` through `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA` to register the extended tests for that invocation:
+
+```sh
+ctest --test-dir build --parallel --output-on-failure
+TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA='--extended' ctest --test-dir build --parallel --output-on-failure
+```
+
+Functional tests have the `functional` label and names like `functional.<script>` or `functional.<script>.<option>`. Extended tests also have the `extended` label. Use CTest filters to select tests:
+
+```sh
+ctest --test-dir build -L '^functional' --parallel --output-on-failure
+ctest --test-dir build -R '^functional\.wallet_' --output-on-failure
+ctest --test-dir build -R '^functional\.rpc_bind\.ipv6$' --output-on-failure
+ctest --test-dir build -L '^functional$' -LE '^extended$' --parallel --output-on-failure
+```
+
+CTest forwards test selection options such as `--exclude` and `--filter`, and child test options such as `--timeout-factor`, through `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA`. Use it for combined logs too:
+
+```sh
+TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA='--combinedlogslen=99999999' ctest --test-dir build -L '^functional$' --output-on-failure
+```
+
+For previous-release compatibility tests, set `PREVIOUS_RELEASES_DIR` to an
+absolute path before downloading releases and running CTest, for example from
+the source root:
+
+```sh
+export PREVIOUS_RELEASES_DIR="$PWD/releases"
+test/get_previous_releases.py
+ctest --test-dir build -L '^functional$' --parallel --output-on-failure
+```
+
+The downloader and both test runners use this setting; otherwise, release lookup
+depends on the working directory.
+
+The suite-level `--coverage` and `--resultsfile` options are not supported through CTest yet and fail explicitly; use the legacy test runner for those workflows. Each CTest invocation clears the fixed shared functional cache and gives each test a fresh temporary directory. Failed test directories are preserved. Do not run concurrent CTest suites in the same build tree because deterministic port seeds do not support that yet.
+
 #### Speed up test runs with a RAM disk
 
 If you have available RAM on your system you can create a RAM disk to use as the `cache` and `tmp` directories for the functional tests in order to speed them up.

+def run_ctest_test(*, config, test, args, combined_logs_len, tmpdirprefix):

+    has_timeout_factor = any(arg.startswith("--timeout-factor=") for arg in test[1:] + args)

+        args.append(f"--timeout-factor={timeout_factor}")

+    # Leave failed test logs intact across reruns, just like the normal runner.

+    args.append(f"--tmpdir={testdir}")
+    # The runner is invoked from the build tree, but execute the test script
+    # from the configured source tree, matching the native test_runner.py's behavior.
+    test_script = os.path.join(
+        config["environment"]["SRCDIR"], "test", "functional", test[0]
+    )
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, test_script] + test[1:] + args,
+        check=False,
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    if result.stderr:
+        print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr, end="")
+

+

+    combined_logs, _ = subprocess.Popen(combined_logs_args, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()
